# Synthetic Lecture 13 — Coagulation

This heading is metadata, not an evidence paragraph.

[EVIDENCE:course_l13_intrinsic_pathway] The intrinsic pathway includes factors XII, XI, IX, and VIII before converging on factor X in the common pathway.

[EVIDENCE:course_l13_extrinsic_pathway] The extrinsic pathway begins with tissue factor and factor VII before converging on factor X in the common pathway.

[EVIDENCE:course_l13_pt] Prothrombin time primarily assesses the extrinsic and common pathways; an isolated factor VII problem can prolong PT while PTT remains normal.

[EVIDENCE:course_l13_ptt] Partial thromboplastin time primarily assesses the intrinsic and common pathways; deficiencies involving factors VIII, IX, XI, or XII can prolong PTT.

[EVIDENCE:course_l13_hemophilia_a] Hemophilia A is factor VIII deficiency. The expected synthetic laboratory pattern is prolonged PTT with normal PT, and factor-deficiency plasma can correct in a mixing study.

[EVIDENCE:course_l13_hit_timing] In this simplified course model, immune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia begins 5 to 10 days after heparin is started and is recognized by a substantial fall in the platelet count.

[EVIDENCE:course_l13_hit_mechanism] Immune heparin-induced thrombocytopenia is caused by antibodies directed against platelet factor 4–heparin complexes. The antibodies activate platelets, so the syndrome is prothrombotic despite thrombocytopenia.

[EVIDENCE:course_l13_dic_pattern] Disseminated intravascular coagulation consumes platelets and coagulation factors. The expected synthetic pattern is thrombocytopenia, prolonged PT and PTT, increased fibrin-degradation products, and reduced fibrinogen.
